chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Al-hukrah (monopolization/hoarding for price control) is not [restricted/defined] except in wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and butter.

key_terms.الْحُكْرَةُ: Monopolization or hoarding of goods to raise prices

ai.seo_question: Which specific food items are subject to price control via monopolization (hukrah) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi explicitly limits the scope of 'al-hukrah' (monopolization) to five staple commodities: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and butter, reflecting the economic priorities of early Islamic society. By restricting this regulation to essential foodstuffs, the Imam establishes a precise jurisprudential boundary for price control mechanisms, distinguishing these necessities from other goods subject to general market forces. This specificity underscores the Shia legal emphasis on protecting the public from scarcity in basic sustenance rather than applying broad monopolistic controls.
